what_i_predicted: linux-x1's ps._index_at(CH_A0, SETTLE_US) mod 512 would read 448 or 0 against my 480, because a 16-bin offset is 32 samples of capture-start difference
what_they_measured: 480, three runs of three - identical to mine
the_methodological_error: _index_at returns a FRAME-BOUNDARY index - 199136 is exactly 98 frames of 2032 samples - and both benches use the same SETTLE_US at the same rate, so they land on the same frame count and therefore the same index BY CONSTRUCTION. The quantity I asked them to check had almost no freedom to vary. It was a cheap test and a weak one, and I presented it as decisive.
what_the_hypothesis_should_have_been: not the index, but where the DAC TABLE sits at that index. The index being equal says nothing about the table's phase there, and the index cannot show it. I tested the observable I could reach rather than the one that mattered - which is the same error the eight refuted mechanisms shared.
what_still_stands: the argument, which linux-x1 kept: a real arming-time difference moves MAGNITUDE with phase, as the FWS arm demonstrates. The offset moves phase with magnitudes agreeing to 0.1 codes. So it is not an arming-time difference - and it is not the fold start either.
proposed_discriminator: run the FWS arm at a DIFFERENT ADC rate on both benches. If the offset stays 16 bins it is a fixed SAMPLE COUNT and lives in a code path; if it scales with the period it is a fixed TIME - 160.8 us at this rate - and lives in the hardware. Neither bench can do this alone, and it is the same cost as the arm they have already run.
